channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: WTI rebounds sharply on fears of renewed escalation in US-Iran war
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures on NYMEX trades 6% higher on the day, slightly above $83.00 during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: US Dollar: Stretched positioning caps gains against peers – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes the US Dollar (USD) enters the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) with strong recent demand but stretched positioning, as cross-border buying and late-July spot demand remain supportive.

item.title: British Pound consolidates against Japanese Yen ahead of central bank decisions
item.description: GBP/JPY extends its subdued price action on Wednesday, forming a series of small-bodied candlesticks after briefly climbing above 219.00 earlier this month, its highest level since December 2007. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 217.50.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Softer CPI keeps RBA on hold – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that Australia’s Q2 Consumer Price Index (CPI) and June headline inflation came in below expectations, easing pressure on the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).

item.title: British Pound languishes below 1.3300 heading into Fed and BoE decisions
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) has given away previous gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday and remains practically flat in the daily chart, trading below 1.3300 and on track to complete a nearly 1.20% decline over the last two weeks.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Hawkish hold could restore Dollar support – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad expects the Federal Open Market Committee to keep the federal funds target range unchanged at 3.50%-3.75% for a fifth consecutive meeting.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Fed risk clouds recovery against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses how the Federal Reserve (Fed) and Bank of Japan (BoJ) decisions could shape USD/JPY, noting that Fed Chair Warsh’s stance on forward guidance adds uncertainty.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed hold to test recent resilience – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole and Frantisek Taborsky expect the Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged, with two dissenters possibly voting for a hike, limiting downside in front-end USD rates.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Moderate pass-through weigh on CHF against Euro – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister analyses how the Swiss National Bank’s recent shift toward tolerating a weaker Swiss Franc affects inflation and EUR/CHF.

item.title: Why is the US Dollar vulnerable when the Federal Reserve is expected to deliver a hawkish hold?
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) stands at a critical juncture as financial markets prepare for the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) upcoming interest rate announcement.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Pressured against US Dollar by softer CPI – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analyst highlight that AUD/USD is offered below 0.6950 after softer June Consumer Price Index (CPI), with markets scaling back expectations for an RBA hike.

item.title: Indian Rupee rally hits pause as oil price recovers strongly, Fed policy awaited
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades marginally lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after a three-day winning streak. The USD/INR pair rebounds to near 95.85, the intraday high, as oil prices have rebounded strongly due to revived geopolitical risks.

item.title: Gold struggles for direction ahead of Federal Reserve policy verdict
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates above $4,000 on Wednesday, as price action remains choppy amid growing caution ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement, while the war in the Middle East intensifies again after a brief lull.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Struggling below 1.1400 with YTD lows at a short distance
item.description: The Euro (EUR) holds marginal gains against the US Dollar on Wednesday after finding some support in the mid-range of the 1.1300s earlier this week but remains unable to find acceptance above 1.1400.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis mulls imposing fees on vessels transiting Southern Red Sea route
item.description: According to a Reuters report, Yemen's Houthis are considering imposing fees on commercial ships sailing through the Southern Red Sea. The report also shows that Houthis might exempt China's shipping fleet from any fee system.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Eases from 0.8575 resistance with the bullish bias intact
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is nursing moderate losses against the British Pound (GBP) on Wednesday, as bulls failed to find acceptance above the 0.8575 resistance area on Tuesday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause guidance – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research notes that the Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep the Federal Funds Target Rate at 3.50%-3.75% at the July FOMC meeting.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC minutes watched for inflation tone – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect the Bank of Canada’s (BoC) Summary of Deliberations to shed light on the July decision, focusing on how policymakers view inflation amid recent energy price moves and Consumer Price Index (CPI) forecast revisions.

item.title: Euro: Seen back toward 1.15 against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that EUR/USD may have bottomed last week if markets maintain a constructive view on further geopolitical de-escalation. He argues a sustained move above 1.15 still requires dovish Federal Reserve (Fed) repricing and stabilised risk sentiment.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Policy gap favours further losses against Euro – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman reports that the Swiss Franc (CHF) continues to weaken versus the Euro, with EUR/CHF reaching new highs as widening yield differentials favour the Euro.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Wednesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $57.92 per troy ounce, up 1.36% from the $57.14 it cost on Tuesday.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Near-term bias remains bearish ahead of Fed-BoE policy
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is marginally higher at around 1.3300 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday. The GBP/USD pair edges up as the US Dollar ticks lower ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement at 18:00 GMT.

item.title: Dow Jones futures gain ahead of Fed policy decision
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain 0.11% to trade around 53,000 during European trading hours on Wednesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures rise 0.16% to trade near 7,480, though Nasdaq 100 futures decline 0.17%, trading near 27,870, respectively.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Softer inflation supports RBA pause – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that weaker-than-expected Australian inflation has sharply reduced market-implied odds of an August RBA rate hike and pushed the AUD lower.

item.title: ECB’s Patsalides: If higher oil prices persist, inflation risks rise
item.description: The remarks from European Central Bank (ECB) policymaker and Governor of the Central Bank of Cyprus, Christodoulos Patsalides, released during the European trading session on Wednesday signal a warning of further acceleration in inflationary pressures if oil prices remain higher.

item.title: Gold stalls intraday recovery near of $4,050 as traders keenly await FOMC decision
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to capitalize on its intraday recovery from an over one-week low and trades below the $4,050 level through the first half of the European session on Wednesday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Surprise risk keeps global rates elevated – ING
item.description: ING’s Michiel Tukker expects the Federal Reserve (Fed) to keep rates on hold, even as markets price a 30% chance of a hike.

item.title: Swiss Franc remains depressed despite brightening ZEW Economic Expectations
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) holds gains near 13-month highs against the Swiss Franc (CHF), with the USD/CHF pair trading a few pips shy of 0.8200, set for a 1.3% monthly rally.

item.title: Equities: Record allocation sustains Dollar exposure – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY reports that global equity allocations have reached a record share of portfolios, with United States (US) markets dominating both equity and fixed-income holdings.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Softer inflation tempers rate hike odds – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that the Australian Dollar, a beneficiary of AI-related demand, has weakened after another softer-than-expected Australian Consumer Price Index (CPI) release.
